Subject: Encoding differences & token billing question

Hi Karthik,

Quick question as we're finalizing our evaluation: Storix is comparing hosted API costs across models and we noticed that token counts for the same prompt vary depending on the tokenizer (SentencePiece vs BPE). Before we sign up for a pilot, can you confirm how Redwood bills tokens when customers use different model families? In particular: 1) Do you normalize counts across model variants for billing or is it raw token usage per-model? 2) If counts differ significantly, do you offer any baseline reconciliation or credits during a pilot?

We're looking at a mix of long-form summarization (avg 2k chars per request) and short chat sessions. If helpful I can send a handful of example prompts and token samples.

Thanks — Oliver
Oliver Grant

Hi Oliver — thanks for the note, good catch. Short answer: Redwood bills based on the tokenizer/token-count produced by the model variant that actually handled the request (i.e., raw token usage per model). That means the same character payload can produce different billed tokens across models.

Long answer and options:
- Raw per-model billing: this is the current hosted API behavior — billed tokens = model-reported tokens (input + output).
- Normalization option: for enterprise pilots we can offer a normalization overlay where we map usage to a chosen reference tokenizer for billing reconciliation (usually the lowest common denominator).
- Pilot credits: we typically provide one-off credits or a blended effective rate for pilots where token-count variance materially affects comparisons.

If you can send sample prompts, Marcus and I will run them across the relevant model family (SentencePiece and a BPE variant) and return a short CSV with token deltas + a cost delta at your current expected rates. Would you like us to include an illustrative ratecard scenario?

Attaching a preliminary ratecard and a token example template — I can set up a short call with Laura (pricing/sales ops) if you want a formal proposal.

Thanks — Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Karthik — thanks for the quick reply and the attachments. That helps. A couple follow-ups after a quick review: 

1) For our evaluation we need apples-to-apples per-token cost comparisons across three model classes (small-chat-bpe, mid-summarizer-sp, and large-chat-sp). If Redwood charges per-model raw tokens, the cost numbers can swing 10–30% simply due to encoder differences.

2) We'd like a pricing proposal that:
   - shows raw per-model billed cost at your standard rates,
   - shows a normalized line (e.g., map all counts to a BPE reference) with an adjusted blended rate, and
   - includes an optional reconciliation clause for the pilot period (one-time adjustment or credit if variance > 12%).

3) Any guidance on recommended model choices for long-form summarization vs short chat in terms of token-efficiency? For example, if SentencePiece gives 15% fewer tokens for long sequences but BPE compresses chat-style sequences better, that will affect our recommended default model.

We are ready to proceed with the pilot next week if we can lock in discounted pilot economics and a simple reconciliation mechanism. Happy to take a 30-minute call with Marcus/Laura to finalize.

— Oliver

Hi Oliver — looping in Marcus and Karthik. I ran the numbers against the samples you sent (see attached token_count_examples.csv). Below is a concise proposal that addresses the three asks you outlined.

Executive summary:
- Billing baseline: Redwood bills per-model raw tokens by default. For the Storix pilot we will provide a blended pilot economics package that maps billed usage to a normalized reference and provides a reconciliation buffer.

Proposal details:
1) Rate presentation
   - Column A: Raw billed cost (per model) — using Standard Hosted rates from Redwood_Hosted_Ratecard_v3.pdf.
   - Column B: Normalized counts mapped to our BPE-reference tokenizer + an adjusted blended rate. This gives you an apples-to-apples cost estimate for decision-making.

2) Pilot reconciliation clause (pilot = 90 days)
   - If average per-request token variance between raw billed tokens and normalized BPE-mapped tokens exceeds 12% over the pilot window, Redwood will issue a one-time credit equal to 75% of the excess token spend above the normalized estimate (applies to the first $250k of billed usage).

3) Recommended model guidance (based on your workload mix)
   - Long-form summarization (2k+ char inputs): use a SentencePiece-optimized summarizer (model-sp-sum-v1) — gives ~12–18% token reduction on our sample inputs vs the BPE baseline and maintains generation quality.
   - Short chat sessions: use chat-optimized BPE variant (model-bpe-chat-v2) for lower latency and comparable token economy on short exchanges.

4) Discount & pilot rate
   - Pilot blended discount: 20% off standard hosted per-token rates for the first 90 days, applied to the normalized billing line.
   - If you commit to a 6-month reserved throughput after the pilot, we'll layer in an additional tiered usage discount.

Operational items:
- We will provide you a small token-counting tool (script + CSV) to pre-check requests against both tokenizers before traffic cutover.
- Marcus will schedule a 30-minute walk-through to show the token-count examples and the proposed ratecard mapping.

Next steps
- Can you confirm the pilot start date (we have availability the week of Mar 29)?
- Please confirm the Storix legal contact for a short pilot contract (we'll circulate a one-page SOW + reconciliation clause).

Thanks — happy to adjust numbers if you prefer a credit cap or a different reconciliation threshold.

Best,
